title: Which cards bring the value close to minus thirty?
description: Six cards with positive and negative numbers are joined by additions and subtractions to reach a value as close to minus thirty as possible. Each card is seen as a move along the number line, and the biggest moves to the left are chosen first. The video breaks the slip of thinking that taking away a card always moves the value to the left.
teaching_notes: One idea: read each card as a move on the number line, then pick the biggest moves to the left until the total reaches the target. Watch for students who think subtraction always moves left, even when a negative card is taken away.

video_script.why: The child builds an expression with a target value by choosing cards as moves on the number line and checking by undoing them.
video_script.substitution: The book's six cards +1, +7, +18, −5, −2, −9, each read as a move along the number line.
video_script.anchor: the six cards of the book laid out in a row above a number line
video_script.payoff_line: The value is exactly minus thirty

final_answer.spoken: minus two plus minus nine, take away eighteen, take away one, which gives minus thirty

never_show: the chosen expression before the steps that build it
maths_rules: left moves: adding a negative card, or taking away a positive card
take away +18 moves 18 left; add −9 moves 9 left; 18 + 9 = 27
30 − 27 = 3, and 3 = 2 + 1: add −2 moves 2 left; take away +1 moves 1 left
video_script.design: The six cards sit above a number line. Each chosen card is shown as an arrow, and the arrows join end to end from zero towards minus thirty.
